assembly_instructions: 1. Fabricate the welded-steel ladder frame from two 7.4 m longitudinal rails, install six crossmembers, then bolt the bumper and rear equipment step to the frame.
2. Install the front steering axle and two rear drive axles, then mount each tire and hub so all tire bottoms sit on the ground plane at y = 0.
3. Fit front and tandem mudguards above the road wheels, then install the cab shell, windshield, side windows, grille slats, headlamps and mirror brackets to the forward chassis mounts.
4. Bolt four hydraulic stabilizer outriggers to the frame rails and pin the square foot pads below them for stationary mast operation.

5. Bolt the EMI shelter floor to the frame, then install the front bulkhead, rear wall, starboard wall and partial port-side lower wall; leave the port upper wall removed and place the roof panel exploded above the shelter as a cutaway reference.
6. Install the two 19-inch receiver racks, power conditioner, cable tray, operator desk, seats, two consoles and displays on the shelter floor while the cutaway side remains open.
7. Slide the named RF receiver, spectrum-analyzer, server, storage and timing trays into the rack faces so the electronics chain is visible from the cutaway side.
8. Route visible coaxial and power trunks from the racks through the cable tray to the telescoping mast base, dish pedestal and auxiliary generator.
9. Bolt the diesel generator to the rear-right frame brackets and connect its power cable to the conditioner rack.
10. Assemble the mast pedestal, three telescoping fiberglass mast sections, guy arms, discone antenna, log-periodic boom with dipoles, and GNSS reference dome.
11. Assemble the azimuth/elevation pedestal, tapered reflector, rim, rear backing plate, feed horn and three feed struts, then cable the dish receiver path back to the RF rack.

12. Perform final continuity checks: every RF antenna connects to the rack, every heavy module connects to the frame or shelter floor, and all stabilizer pads contact the ground before raising the mast.

info.japanese_name: 電磁妨害状況把握装置2型
info.english_name: Electromagnetic Interference Situation Awareness Device, Type 2
info.summary: Truck-mounted version of the JASDF satellite EM-interference monitoring system, built by NEC and carried on eight Isuzu GIGA heavy trucks.
info.description: Type 2 is the mobile variant of the 電磁妨害状況把握装置 family — a system Japan's Ministry of Defense procures to monitor electromagnetic interference targeting Japanese artificial satellites and to train and evaluate Air Self-Defense Force responses to jamming of communications satellites. Where Type 1 is a fixed ground installation, Type 2 is deployable: the sensor chain, signal-processing racks, and operator consoles ride in a shelter on a large Isuzu truck, letting units move the receiver close to the region of interest or disperse for survivability. The main equipment contract went to NEC in FY2022, and eight Isuzu GIGA trucks were contracted separately in FY2023 as the prime-mover platform.

facts.label: Scale model length
facts.value: 7.6 m overall scene length, representative of a heavy Isuzu GIGA equipment truck.

facts.label: Shelter envelope
facts.value: 4.2 m long × 2.4 m wide × 2.2 m high EMI equipment shelter with port-side cutaway.

facts.label: Mast height
facts.value: Three telescoping mast sections shown to 5.9 m above ground for elevated RF survey antennas.

facts.label: Wheelbase layout
facts.value: Three-axle heavy truck layout with front steering axle and tandem rear drive axles.

facts.label: Dish aperture
facts.value: 1.0 m class steerable Ku-band monitoring dish represented as a tapered shallow reflector with rim and feed struts.

facts.label: Rack standard
facts.value: Two 0.6 m wide 19-inch equipment racks are broken into receiver, analyzer, server, storage and timing trays.

facts.label: Stabilizer span
facts.value: Four deployed stabilizer pads span about 4.2 m across the vehicle for static mast operation.

facts.label: Cab width
facts.value: Cab details fit within a 2.35 m wide forward-control heavy-truck envelope.

facts.label: Procured vehicles
facts.value: Eight Isuzu GIGA trucks contracted for the mobile Type 2 platform.

facts.label: Operational role
facts.value: Detect, characterise and train response to electromagnetic interference against Japanese communications satellites.
